entries.title: A hacker racks up a $45,000 AWS bill for their victim, only to generate $800 worth of Monero
entries.body: A hacker gained access to someone's Amazon Web Services account and used it to spin up servers to run Monero <button class="define-target" id="mining">miners</button>, ultimately netting 6 Monero (XMR) worth a total of about $800 over the couple of weeks they were running. All this work, however, cost the hacked individual about $45,000 in AWS fees, providing a particularly salient example of why people don't typically use AWS to mine crypto. Fortunately, Amazon waived the bill for the owner of the compromised account.

links.linkText: "$45,000 AWS Crypto-Mining Hack Generates $800 of Monero"

entries.body: Stolen <button class="define-target" id="private-key">private keys</button> from the blockchain gaming platform Vulcan Forged enabled attackers to siphon funds out of just shy of 100 user wallets. Rather than users managing their own private keys, this is done by the platform, suggesting the issue was not user error. The project says it plans to reimburse users.

entries.title: 8ight Finance completely drained after private key leak
entries.body: A compromised <button class="define-target" id="private-key">private key</button> allowed an attacker to remove all funds from 8ight Finance's treasury, amounting to about $1.75 million. The team admitted to sending the key through Facebook chat and Google Drive, writing, "This is our first project, so we must admit our opsec [operational security] was low."

links.linkText: "8ight Finance Hacked: All Funds in Treasury Withdrawn due to Leak of the Private Key"

entries.body: Polygon lost a bit over $2 million after a hacker exploited a bug involving a lack of balance/allowance check in their MRC20 <button class="define-target" id="smart-contract">contract</button>. Polygon had been in the process of releasing a patch for the vulnerability, which had been reported by a white-hat hacker, and released an emergency upgrade the following day. The silent, zero-warning <button class="define-target" id="fork">hard fork</button> raised some eyebrows, and Polygon didn't release details until several weeks later. Polygon ultimately paid about $3.5 million in bug bounties to two white-hat hackers who submitted reports, which was far less than the total value of Polygon's $MATIC tokens, all 9.2 billion of which (worth around $24 billion) could have been stolen by an attacker using this vulnerability.

entries.title: Hackers steal about $200 million from BitMart
entries.body: BitMart, "the most trusted cryptocurrency trading platform", experienced a major breach in which attackers stole approximately $200 million of various cryptocurrencies. The CEO attributed the exploit to a stolen <button class="define-target" id="private-key">private key</button>, and promised to compensate users who were impacted.

entries.title: $120 million is stolen from BadgerDAO
entries.body: A hacker was able to use a compromised Cloudflare API key to inject malicious code into the BadgerDAO platform via Cloudflare Workers. They then siphoned currency of various kinds, equivalent to approximately $120 million, out of user accounts over approximately two weeks before being discovered.

links.linkText: "Hacked Cryptocurrency Platform Begs Hacker to Please Return $119 Million"

entries.title: NFT collecter friesframe has a Bored Ape and several other valuable NFTs stolen
entries.body: Although friesframe had transferred some of his valuable NFTs to <button class="define-target" id="cold-wallet">cold storage</button> (a crypto wallet not connected to the Internet), he had been waiting for <button class="define-target" id="gas">gas fees</button> to come down before transferring more. In that period, his hot wallet was hacked, and a Bored Ape NFT and several others were stolen.

entries.body: A hacker stole $31 million from the <button class="define-target" id="liquidity-pool">liquidity pool</button> provider MonoX by exploiting a bug in their <button class="define-target" id="smart-contract">smart contract</button> software that allowed them to exchange a token for itself and artificially inflate the price. MonoX took the classic approach of those burned by crypto issues, and tried to get the cash back by... asking nicely.
entries.title: $31 million stolen from MonoX in smart contract bug

entries.body: An attacker fooled a developer of the bZx <button class="define-target" id="defi">decentralized finance</button> platform into opening a Word document with a malicious macro, which ran a script that gave the attackers access to the developer's crypto wallet <button class="define-target" id="private-key">private keys</button>. They were able to gain access not only the developer's personal wallet keys, but to two keys to bZx wallets. The attacker made off with approximately $55 million. bZx subsequently tried to offer the attacker a bounty to return the funds, though they were not successful.
entries.title: Hacker steals around $55 million from bZx
